_comment: The claims file (#915 Wave 3). It replaces tests/claims.json and holds ONLY what a machine cannot derive: the qualities x surfaces vocabulary, the lane registry, the claim rows with their severity and the date each was last demonstrated red, the law registry, the consent ledger, the join laws, the deliberate n/a cells with their reasons, and the flow ownership + minimumTests floors. Owners, journeys, budgets, seeds, engines, fuzz targets and Vitest projects are DERIVED at read time by scripts/test-report/derive.mjs from the roster, the Stryker configs, scripts/mutation/seeds.mjs, scripts/fuzz/targets.mjs and vitest.config.ts — see TESTING.md.
_why: tests/claims.json was 252 KB of hand-typed grid whose per-cell assessments duplicated what the lanes already proved. #915 keeps the declarations (a claim, a law, a reason for an absence) and derives the observations.

severity.S2: Silent wrongness — the product does the wrong thing and says nothing.
severity.S3: A promise degraded — slower, noisier, or partly unproven.
severity.S4: Fidelity, or blocked on something outside the repo.

claims.name: rust supply-chain gate
claims.evidence: cargo-audit and cargo-deny per crate; the guarded skip is loud and --require turns a missing binary red

demonstratedRed.seed: disable the available-but-did-not-run check in decideExit
demonstratedRed.failure: 'AVAILABLE BUT DID NOT RUN fails' goes red — an unrun lane reads as a pass

claims.name: rust unsafe-edge ratchet
claims.evidence: an unjustified or unledgered unsafe site fails; the count is tighten-only in both directions

demonstratedRed.seed: plant an unjustified `unsafe` block in packages/tunnel/data-plane/src
demonstratedRed.failure: exit 1 naming the unjustified site and the ledger overrun

claims.name: dependency behaviour and CI egress ratchets
claims.evidence: install-time code digested over the command AND the script bytes, so a republished tarball at the same version fails; CI egress debt shrinks only

demonstratedRed.seed: drop the unledgered-package push and the stale-entry push from lifecycle-audit.mjs
demonstratedRed.failure: an unledgered dependency declaring postinstall passes, and a ledger entry for a dependency that no longer runs install-time code is never noticed

claims.name: nightly red blocks release
claims.evidence: blocks release preparation when a nightly red issue is open

demonstratedRed.seed: publish-guards returns an open nightly restore/export failure issue

claims.name: total product role lowering
claims.evidence: every registered role has an explicit lowering

demonstratedRed.seed: remove one profile lowering from the product role registry
demonstratedRed.failure: the role registry reports the missing lowering before emit

demonstratedRed.seed: delete one interaction recipe or omit a required state
demonstratedRed.failure: the recipe inventory or state contract test fails

demonstratedRed.seed: add a raw color, font, size, weight, or radius to a shipped CSS consumer
demonstratedRed.failure: the design-token ratchet reports the exact consumer regression

demonstratedRed.seed: point one shipped catalog entry at an unregistered icon key
demonstratedRed.failure: the shared icon registry rejects the catalog drift

demonstratedRed.seed: change the shared byte or relative-time formatter in one client lane
demonstratedRed.failure: the canonical formatter contract fails before clients diverge

demonstratedRed.seed: emit a retired alias or omit a required shell/blueprint token
demonstratedRed.failure: the profile contract parity test rejects the emitter drift

removedMinimumTestsFlows._comment: One-shot retirement markers. Each entry retires a flow whose owner file was deleted with nothing to carry its floor. scripts/test-report/ratchet-floors.mjs validates a marker only while it is new against the base, so a marker is inert once landed and is dropped by the next change set that touches this file (#1120 dropped the 21 already spent on the trunk).

flows.name: Concurrent tabs share one canonical intent result
flows.approvedMinimumTestsDeviation: #996 W5 deleted the IndexedDB outbox and with it multi-writer.contract.test.ts (three tab-coordinator cases over fake-indexeddb). The queue-level contract those cases named — one canonical intent id, concurrent retry serialized to one successor, Web Lock boundary — lives in intents.contract.test.ts. Floor stays 3.

flows.name: Opening, renaming and managing an installed app from Home
flows.approvedMinimumTestsDeviation: #799 stage 2 deleted the app builder and apps/desktop/tests/e2e/builder.spec.ts with it: five of desktop-builder-journey's six cases (palette Create, streamed builder turn, failed Publish, Preview iframe, Code tab, Cloud Logs) drove surfaces that no longer exist. Its one surviving premise — reaching an installed app and acting on it from Home — is already exercised by onboarding-home.spec.ts's app-lifecycle half (open a tile, open from the palette, rename, the tile context menu, the Photos seat), so the floor of 6 transfers here rather than evaporating. onboarding-home.spec.ts declares 18 cases against a combined floor of 19; the split names which duties each flow carries.

flows.name: Installable web app boot and session lifecycle
Auto-founded gateway → pair ticket → phone joins Shared (#603)
Announcements, modal focus, keyboard focus, native control labels, Dynamic Type, and virtualized reading order
cargo-audit / cargo-deny run per crate, and an unrun lane never reads as a pass
Every Rust unsafe site is justified and ledgered, tighten-only
SBOM, provenance and release-manifest signature verify or refuse
Install-time code and CI egress ratchets only shrink
A row queued while offline shows its pending state across a PWA reload
flows.approvedMinimumTestsDeviation: Takes over the retired `web-pending-overlay` floor one-to-one. That journey proved the PWA recovers a VISIBLE pending row across a reload while still offline, and it drove Tally, Tasks and Agenda — the three interfaces #831 cleared, which left it without a subject on this seat. Rather than keep two near-identical offline journeys over the one remaining app that renders the shared pending overlay, the contract moved into `offline-reconnect.spec.ts`, which was itself retargeted from Tasks to Docs in the same change: it now asserts the optimistic title AND its `.kit-pending-chip` survive the offline reload before going on to prove settlement on reconnect. Two named contracts over one journey, exactly as `desktop-real-journey` and `desktop-app-open-journey` share `onboarding-home.spec.ts`. Same surface, dimension, tier and floor; no assertion dropped. #834 rebuilt Agenda, Notes and Tasks and did NOT move the contract back: one PWA offline journey over Docs still owns both halves, and the rebuilt apps' own pending honesty is proven at the boot tier (packages/blueprints/src/app-boot/agenda.test.ts) rather than by re-splitting this flow.

surface.vault-core.offline.restated: Skip: vault is a storage primitive; offline UX is exercised by mobile.offline + web.offline consuming surfaces.

surface.vault-core.journey.restated: Skip: no end-user vault journey surface; blank-machine restore owns backup-restore.journey and search/enrichment flows own vault correctness paths.

surface.blob-custody.offline.restated: Skip: blob store has no offline user journey; durability is ENOSPC custody + disk-full e2e; offline is a consuming-surface concern.

surface.blob-custody.compat.restated: Skip: no blob format migration path in v0; CBSF mutation + format floors cover format stability instead.

surface.blob-custody.journey.restated: Skip: custody is a primitive; journeys live on mobile upload durability and desktop/gateway blob consumers.

surface.backup-restore.concurrency.restated: Skip: restore into a LIVE gateway was deleted with the founding plane (#603) — restore is the offline `recover` verb, so concurrent restore has no surface.

surface.backup-restore.offline.restated: Skip: restore is an online blank-machine operation; offline continuity is owned by vault WAL + mobile offline, not backup kit.

surface.gateway.offline.restated: Skip: gateway is always the online host; offline UX lives on mobile/web clients. No meaningful gateway-offline matrix cell.

surface.gateway.compat.restated: Skip: no gateway wire migration suite in v0; protocol judge + tunnel wire contracts own compatibility pressure.

surface.app-engine.offline.restated: Skip: app-engine runs server-side with the gateway; offline is a client-surface dimension.

surface.app-engine.compat.restated: Skip: no app-engine API migration surface in v0; harness registry contracts own kind-compat pressure.

surface.app-engine.journey.restated: Skip: user journeys are desktop/web/mobile copilot paths; engine is exercised via agent-runtime.journey (fake-acp).

surface.automations.offline.restated: Skip: automations schedule on the gateway host; offline client behavior is mobile/web. No offline scheduler product path.

surface.automations.compat.restated: Skip: no automations schema migration in v0; scheduler mutation floors cover pure compute stability.

surface.agent-runtime.offline.restated: Skip: harnesses require a live CLI/ACP process; offline is not a runtime dimension (client offline owns UX).

surface.extension.durability.restated: Structural N/A: the extension owns no durable state; paired credentials are browser storage and gateway-owned.

surface.extension.concurrency.restated: Structural N/A for v0: one active popup/worker transaction is admitted per browser profile.

surface.extension.performance.restated: Structural N/A for v0: the companion performs no user-visible compute or transfer hot path.

surface.extension.scalability.restated: Structural N/A for v0: one companion serves one browser profile; fleet scale belongs to the gateway.

surface.extension.compat.restated: Structural N/A until a versioned extension storage format exists; gateway protocol contracts own wire compatibility.

surface.oauth-worker.durability.restated: Structural N/A: the OAuth courier intentionally holds no durable application state.

surface.oauth-worker.concurrency.restated: Structural N/A: stateless Cloudflare Worker isolates provide request concurrency; no shared mutable state exists.

surface.oauth-worker.performance.restated: Structural N/A: provider and edge latency dominate the stateless one-shot code courier.

surface.oauth-worker.scalability.restated: Structural N/A: Cloudflare owns isolate scaling and the courier holds no application queue or pool.

surface.oauth-worker.offline.restated: Structural N/A: an edge OAuth callback service has no offline product mode.

surface.oauth-worker.compat.restated: Structural N/A: the courier exposes one versionless, short-lived exchange contract owned by contract tests.

surface.oauth-worker.journey.restated: Structural N/A: end-user OAuth journeys are owned by the consuming desktop/web surfaces; the worker is a stateless courier.
